learningObjectives: Trace voluntary movement from cortical planning to spinal execution.
Distinguish basal-ganglia action selection from cerebellar error correction.
Relate upper- and lower-motor-neuron signs to pathway level.
Avoid treating all reduced movement as weakness.

anatomy.label: Premotor and supplementary cortex
anatomy.detail: These frontal regions prepare movements using internal goals and external cues.
anatomy.clinical: Disruption may cause impaired sequencing, initiation or apraxic errors.

anatomy.label: Primary motor cortex
anatomy.detail: M1 contributes fractionated voluntary control through corticospinal and corticobulbar projections.
anatomy.clinical: Focal injury commonly produces contralateral weakness and loss of fine control.

anatomy.label: Basal ganglia
anatomy.detail: Parallel loops facilitate useful actions while suppressing competitors.
anatomy.clinical: Circuit imbalance contributes to bradykinesia, rigidity, dystonia and hyperkinesia.

anatomy.label: Cerebellum
anatomy.detail: Cerebellar circuits compare intended and actual outcomes to refine timing and accuracy.
anatomy.clinical: Lesions cause ipsilateral ataxia, dysmetria and impaired motor learning.

anatomy.label: Brainstem and spinal cord
anatomy.detail: Descending pathways converge on interneurons and lower motor neurons.
anatomy.clinical: Damage may produce weakness, altered tone, abnormal reflexes or patterned posturing.

interaction.title: Explore the Motor System
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Plan
stages.text: Frontal networks define the goal and organise the action sequence.

stages.label: Select
stages.text: Basal-ganglia loops bias the chosen action and suppress competitors.

stages.label: Command
stages.text: Motor cortex sends descending signals through brainstem and spinal pathways.

stages.label: Correct
stages.text: Cerebellar prediction and sensory feedback continuously refine the movement.

stages.label: Learn
stages.text: Successful and unsuccessful outcomes update future motor commands.

quizBank.question: Which structure is most associated with online prediction-error correction?
quizBank.explanation: The cerebellum compares expected and actual movement outcomes and updates commands.

quizBank.question: The corticospinal tract is especially important for:
quizBank.explanation: Corticospinal projections are central to skilled voluntary control, particularly of distal limbs.

quizBank.question: Basal-ganglia circuits primarily help to:
options: Bias action selection and movement vigour
quizBank.explanation: Basal-ganglia loops help select and scale actions while suppressing competitors.

quizBank.question: An upper-motor-neuron lesion commonly produces:
options: Weakness with increased tone and reflexes
quizBank.explanation: Loss of descending control can produce weakness, hyperreflexia and spasticity.

quizBank.question: Apraxia refers to:
options: Impaired learned action despite sufficient basic strength
quizBank.explanation: Apraxia is a disorder of learned purposeful action not explained by elementary weakness alone.
